identificationModule.briefTitle: Creatine or Vitamin D Supplementation in Persons With Spinal Cord Injury Undergoing Resistance Training
identificationModule.officialTitle: Creatine or Vitamin D Supplementation in Persons With Spinal Cord Injury Undergoing Resistance Training

descriptionModule.briefSummary: The purpose of this study is to determine the effects of creatine monohydrate or vitamin D supplementation on strength gains following a traditional resistance training program for adults with spinal cord injury.

armGroups.label: Placebo
armGroups.description: Daily supplementation with 3g of dextrose during eight weeks and placebo ampoules each two weeks.

armGroups.label: Creatine
armGroups.description: Daily supplementation with 3g of monohydrate creatine during eight weeks. Placebo ampoules each two weeks.

armGroups.label: Vitamin D
armGroups.description: Daily supplementation with 3g of dextrose during eight weeks. Vitamin D supplementation, 25000 IU each two weeks.

interventions.name: Creatine
interventions.description: Daily supplementation with 3g of monohydrate creatine during 8 weeks

interventions.name: Vitamin D
interventions.description: Vitamin D supplementation with 25000 IU each two weeks during eight weeks

primaryOutcomes.description: Triceps, Biceps, Subscapular and Iliac crest

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Spinal cord injury
* Minimum time since injury: 3 months

Exclusion Criteria:

* Participation in resistance training programmes in the previous 6 months
* Creatine or vitamin D supplementation in the previous 6 months
